A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RF-Solver/RF-Edit work, with readable text, equations, figures, and tables supporting reliable comparison. The supplied v1 ends with references despite mentioning an appendix; v3 includes readable Appendices A–F. Settings newly documented there can be distinguished from explicitly revised settings.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation, image/video reconstruction, and editing experiments in Tables 1–4, together with quantitative and qualitative ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results, adds sampler comparisons in Tables 1–2, and presents additional stylized-generation and video-editing results in its appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 changes the finite-difference offset used to estimate the velocity derivative from half the current integration interval in v1 to a fixed 0.01 in v3. This revises the derivative-estimation procedure within the retained Taylor-expansion solver. RF-Edit retains its value-feature-sharing mechanism; the HunyuanVideo implementation applies that mechanism to another backbone.

E1.justification: v3 adds demonstrated reference-style-conditioned generation with new content prompts in Figure 8 and video object insertion, such as adding a Santa hat, in Figure 9. These extend the displayed scenarios beyond v1's video replacement/global edits. The principal COCO generation/reconstruction and image/video editing coverage remains.

E2.justification: v1's generation and reconstruction tables compare RF-Solver only against vanilla RF. v3 adds DPM-Solver++ and RF-Heun to generation in Table 1, and RF-Heun to both image and video reconstruction in Table 2. These introduce substantive higher-order solver comparisons central to evaluating RF-Solver. The editing comparator sets in Tables 3–4 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v1 specifies 10 generation steps for RF-Solver, requiring 20 NFE, and 30 inversion/reconstruction steps, requiring 60 NFE per pass. v3 Appendix B instead reports budgets of 10 and 50 NFE, respectively. Added experiments use Stable Diffusion for the DPM-Solver comparison and HunyuanVideo for editing. Captioning is reported as GPT-4o rather than GPT-4.0. These are reported protocol changes; they do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendices D–E add qualitative case studies of reference-style preservation across different prompts and transfer of the editing framework to HunyuanVideo. The existing Taylor-order and feature-sharing-step ablations remain. v1 Figure 8 becomes v3 Figure 7 with the same examples; its new caption identifies the existing no-sharing row rather than establishing a newly added ablation.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. Both present point estimates and qualitative examples.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 2, and 5 revise results and add comparator entries. Generation FID changes from 26.55 to 25.33 for RF and from 25.45 to 23.98 for RF-Solver. RF-Solver reconstruction MSE changes from 0.0094 to 0.0092 for images and 0.0139 to 0.0134 for videos. New Heun/DPM results and appendix examples expand the evidence. Tables 3–4 are numerically unchanged. Changed budgets and derivative settings prevent interpreting revised scores as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1 reverses v1's incorrectly signed finite-difference numerator to agree with the derivative formula already stated in v1. Section 3.3 also revises the feature-sharing index range from n through N to N−n through N. The Taylor derivation and claimed local error order are otherwise retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a training-free Taylor-based RF sampler that improves inversion/reconstruction and a feature-sharing editing framework that preserves source structure across image and video tasks. The broader compatibility claim also persists. Removing the contribution bullets and adding HunyuanVideo evidence do not materially redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly emphasizes inversion's dependence on prompt quality and motivates detailed GPT-4o captions. Appendix F discusses prospective applications to other generation, restoration, and editing systems. The existing interpretations of higher-order solver tradeoffs and excessive feature sharing remain, including their stated failure mechanisms.

D1.justification: Appendix B supplies substantial previously undocumented information: sharing the last 19 FLUX single blocks and 14 OpenSora blocks, about 40 inversion videos, over 300 editing images, DIV2K/social-media/generated-image sources, 2–3 target prompts per image, generation resolution, and baseline implementation sources. Appendix E identifies HunyuanVideo's sharing location. The project code link remains unchanged, while v1's single-A100/40GB hardware specification is removed.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands the cited context around numerical inversion and sampling, newer rectified-flow/generation models, and editing applications, including DPM-Solver++, BELM, exact DPM-Solver inversion, and HunyuanVideo. Appendix F adds connections to further application areas. Section 2.1 also removes v1's claim that RF-Inversion's improvement primarily stems from source-image information leakage, emphasizing direct vector-field error reduction instead.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially rewritten around the reconstruction-error analysis, related work is condensed, and method explanations are reorganized. Contribution bullets disappear, most experimental setup moves into Appendix B, and appendices organize pseudocode, examples, and potential applications. Abstract, captions, and experimental prose receive extensive editing beyond isolated wording corrections.

P2.justification: v3 adds large stylized-generation and video-editing displays, expands Tables 1–2, and transposes Table 1's structure. Figure 2 moves into the introduction, Algorithm 1 moves to Appendix A, and v1's generation Figure 5 becomes appendix Figure 10. Figure captions and pipeline labels are revised, alongside extensive reflow into the conference layout. Retained editing and ablation images are reused.

improvement.justification: The added Heun comparisons provide more informative validation than v1's Euler-only solver comparisons, while the pseudocode correction and appendix settings improve reproducibility. These are useful net gains, with limits: the DPM comparison uses a different backbone, changed budgets prevent direct cross-version performance attribution, and hardware information is lost. The revision strengthens evaluation and documentation without substantially changing the established contributions.
